title: Search Result Thumbnail & Rich Snippet Image
author: Namias
description: Add Search Result Thumbnails (image in rich snippets) to improve Click-Through Rate (CTR) in Google search results. When users search for 'Keneth Namias' or the portfolio website, Google will display a thumbnail image next to the search result, making it more visually appealing and credible.
problemStatement: Currently, search results for 'Keneth Namias' or the portfolio website show text-only results without images. This results in lower CTR compared to results that include thumbnails. Search Result Thumbnails catch the user's eye and make the result look more credible.
goals: Display thumbnail images in Google search results for portfolio-related queries
Improve Click-Through Rate (CTR) from search results
Ensure images meet Google's recommended dimensions (1200x630px minimum)
Maintain consistent branding across search results and social previews
Support different images for different content types (person, projects, blog posts)
nonGoals: Changes to Google's search algorithm or ranking
Real-time image updates in search results (Google caches these)
Support for all possible rich result types (focus on Person, Article, CreativeWork)

technicalRequirements: JSON-LD structured data must validate with Google's Rich Results Test
Images must be at least 1200x630 pixels (Google recommendation)
Images must be accessible via public URL (no auth required)
og:image and twitter:image meta tags must be present on all pages
Image alt text must be descriptive for accessibility
Images should use WebP format with JPEG fallback for compatibility

risks.risk: Google may not display thumbnail even with valid schema
risks.mitigation: Ensure images meet all Google guidelines; monitor Google Search Console
Use versioned image URLs; request re-indexing after major changes

risks.risk: Large images may slow page load
risks.mitigation: Use Next.js Image component with proper sizing; implement lazy loading

successMetrics: Google Rich Results Test passes for all schema types
og:image and twitter:image meta tags present on all pages
No structured data errors in Google Search Console
CTR improvement visible in Google Search Console (after 2-4 weeks)
